audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers read [Skill, Sion, Sion, Skill, Skill, Sion, Sion]; the packet reads [Sion, Skill, Skill, Skill, Malphite, Skill, Skill].
audit.why: The page's own whys track the packet, not its tokens: whys[0] says he is one of the weakest level-1 duelists (Sion), whys[1] ends 'keeping it genuinely even' (Skill) while the token said Sion, and whys[4] says 'Malphite owns the all-in threat' while the token said Skill. Level 1 is the one row Sion actually owns outright, and level 6 is the one row Malphite does.
audit.corrected: Six rows flipped as matched full/content pairs to the packet: L1 Sion, L2 Skill, L3 Skill, L6 Malphite, 1st item Skill, 2+ items Skill. L4-5 already agreed.

audit.whatIsWrong: mid calls Unstoppable Force 'an instant knockup with global range'.
audit.why: It is 1000 range — he has to be within a screen of you and he travels there, which is exactly why hugging a wall or holding your own R for the counter-engage works. 'Global' tells the player the positioning advice is pointless. The 130s figure the page gives is correct at rank 1.
audit.corrected: Range corrected to 1000 in mid, whys[4] and spikes[1].text, with the 130s kept.

audit.whatIsWrong: late calls his W an 'armor aura', and nothing on the page connects Sion's armour shred to Malphite's damage.
audit.why: Thunderclap is an attack-based effect that creates aftershocks in front of him — an auto-attack reset that applies on-hit, not an aura, and it is the brief's autoreset-burst-tell and onhit-itemization flag. The decisive interaction the page misses is that Ground Slam deals magic damage BASED ON HIS ARMOR, so Roar of the Slayer's armour shred cuts his damage output at the same time it cuts his durability — order the casts shred-first and the whole trade changes. The mirrored malphite__sion audit records the same finding from the other side.
audit.corrected: Ground Slam's armour scaling and the shred-first sequencing written into mid and late; Seismic Shard restated as stealing move speed for 3 seconds on a flat 8s cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags 'NO cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere' and it is accurate — no ability on the page carries a number except the 130s ult.
audit.why: His two lane abilities are flat cooldowns at every rank: Seismic Shard 8s, Ground Slam 7s. That is what makes his poke feel constant and it is the number that tells you there is no long punish window before 6 — the punish is Granite Shield instead, which recharges only if he goes untouched.
audit.corrected: Both cooldowns written into whys[1] and mid, with Granite Shield's recharge condition kept as the real early lever.

edits.before: Charged Q from brush/fog is a half-HP knockup. Only take the trade when Malphite's Unstoppable Force is down.
edits.after: Charged Q from brush is a half-HP knockup, but Seismic Shard steals your move speed on a flat 8s cooldown.

edits.before: Heartsteel is your spike â€” force fights the moment it completes, on Unstoppable Force's cooldown.
edits.after: Heartsteel is your spike - but force fights only while Unstoppable Force sits on its 130s cooldown.

edits.before: Both champions have their full basic kits but neither has a power spike — Malphite can Q-slow to reduce your engage window, and careful footwork lets him regenerate his passive shield, keeping it genuinely even.
edits.after: Neither side has a power spike at 2 — Seismic Shard steals your move speed for 3 seconds on a flat 8s cooldown, and a few untouched seconds regenerate Granite Shield, keeping it genuinely even.

edits.before: Unstoppable Force is instant, undodgeable, and knocks you up with zero telegraph time — Malphite owns the all-in threat the moment this cooldown is available, and you must play off the wall and track its timer.
edits.after: Unstoppable Force launches him 1000 units into a knockup you cannot sidestep, on 130s at rank 1 — from 6 the all-in is his whenever it is up, so hug the wall and count it down after every use.

edits.before: Heartsteel's HP compound makes your W-shield enormous, your E-shred strips his armor before every trade, and his AP damage output hasn't scaled to match your bulk — the lane tilts back your way off first item.
edits.after: Heartsteel makes your W-shield enormous and Roar of the Slayer strips the armour Ground Slam's damage is calculated from, cutting his output as well as his bulk — but his R still decides fights, so the stage stays contested.

edits.before: Malphite's Unstoppable Force comes online as the first all-in threat — respect the engage angle and track his position; your own R can counter-engage or disengage if he dives you.
edits.after: Unstoppable Force comes online as his first all-in threat — 1000 range, a knockup you cannot dodge, 130s at rank 1. Track it and keep your own R for the counter-engage or the escape.

edits.before: Levels 4 through 6 are the matchup's gray zone. Malphite stacks armor quietly, and your Q does physical damage — if he itemizes armor early (Bramble Vest into Sunfire), your trades start to feel weaker than they should. Don't let him freely regenerate his passive shield between poke intervals; keep consistent Q-threat on the wave so he has to choose between farming and refreshing the shield. His level 6 Unstoppable Force is the first time he genuinely flips the script — it's an instant knockup with global range on a 130-second cooldown. Track it carefully, play slightly back off the wall when the cooldown is back up, and keep your own R available to re-engage or peel if he dives you with jungle follow-up.
edits.after: Levels 4 through 6 are the matchup's gray zone. Seismic Shard is a flat 8s and Ground Slam a flat 7s, so his chip never really stops — but Ground Slam's damage is calculated from his ARMOR, which means your Roar of the Slayer shred cuts his damage at the same time as his durability. Shred first, then trade. Don't let him regenerate Granite Shield between poke intervals; keep constant Q-threat so he must choose between farming and refreshing it. His level 6 Unstoppable Force is the first real flip — a 1000-range charge into an unavoidable knockup on 130 seconds. Track it, play off the wall while it is up, and keep your own R for the re-engage or the peel.

edits.before: Your late game is a nightmare for Malphite's design: he stacks armor to reduce physical damage, but your W-shield's value scales with your max HP, your E shreds his armor before every trade, and your zombie passive forces him to disengage or absorb free damage even when you die. The only late threat is that his magic-damage kit — Q slow, W armor aura, R knockup — doesn't care how much HP you have, so build one MR item (Hollow Radiance works perfectly into him as a tank) to deny his AP scaling. With anti-magic coverage, you are simply unkillable in this matchup and he becomes a slow, low-damage speedbump you zone for free.
edits.after: Your late game is a nightmare for Malphite's design: he stacks armour to reduce physical damage, but your W-shield's value scales with your max HP, your E shreds the armour his Ground Slam damage is calculated from, and your zombie passive forces him to disengage or absorb free damage even when you die. The live threat is that Seismic Shard, Ground Slam and Unstoppable Force are all magic damage that ignores how much HP you stacked, so build one MR item (Hollow Radiance works perfectly into him as a tank) to deny his scaling. With that coverage you are effectively unkillable here and he becomes a slow speedbump you zone for free.

notes: Two things worth flagging beyond the edits. First, the chart was wrong on six of seven rows in both layers while the prose already described the packet's version — the level-1 row in particular said Skill on a stage the page itself calls one of the weakest level 1s in the game. Second, the interaction that decides this lane was absent: Ground Slam's damage is based on Malphite's Armor, so Sion's armour shred is offence as well as defence, and the cast order matters. That matches what the mirrored malphite__sion audit recorded from the other side. The packet's suspectName 'Reach Unstoppable Force' is a false positive — that is the correct name of his R. Full-layer strings carry mojibake em dashes; before-strings copied byte-for-byte and replacements use plain hyphens.
